source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Nameless, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; named, it is the mother of the myriad things.
Therefore, constantly without desire, one observes its subtle mystery,
constantly with desire, one observes its boundary;
These two arise together but have different names; together they are called the mysterious.
Mystery upon mystery: the gate of all subtle wonders.
When all under Heaven know beauty as beauty, there is already ugliness.
When all know good as good, there is already non-good.

Thus being and non-being give birth to one another; difficult and easy complete one another; long and short compare one another; high and low lean on one another; music and sound harmonize with one another; before and after follow one another.
Therefore the sage deals with affairs by non-action,
and carries out teaching without words; the myriad things arise, and he does not refuse them; they are born, and he does not possess them; he acts, and does not rely on them.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical route or track for travel.
Sentence Translations (English): The great road runs through the fields.
A forked path lies ahead.
The road is rough and long.
He follows the road and goes on.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To utter words or explain something verbally.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This is the verbal sense distinct from the noun.
Sentence Translations (English): The Master did not speak of it.
The matter is hard to express.
I do not dare speak its name.
What a gentleman speaks of.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fundamental path, principle, or reality underlying all things; in this context, the Dao that can be spoken of is not the constant Dao.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it refers to the ultimate principle rather than an ordinary road or method.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used after a verb to indicate that something can be accepted or considered suitable.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often carries a judgment of fitness or acceptability.
Sentence Translations (English): This statement may be adopted.
The plan may be used.
Proceed only when it is acceptable.
The affair must not be neglected.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses possibility or capability: something is able to be spoken or treated in a certain way.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks capacity or permissibility, not a completed action.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A general negative particle denying a statement or predicate.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used in direct denial or correction.
Sentence Translations (English): This is not my intention.
This is not a good plan.
It cannot last.
It is not known to people.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative prefix or particle indicating absence, denial, or contrary status.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks contrast or exclusion rather than simple verbal negation in many set phrases.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The enduring, unchanging Dao as opposed to a named or spoken version of it.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Refers to the abiding Dao, not a habitual path or ordinary doctrine.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To give a designation to something or speak its name.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Verbal sense parallel to the noun.
Sentence Translations (English): It cannot be named.
He names it Dao.
Everyone calls it so.
It cannot yet be named.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A word or designation used to identify or classify something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it contrasts with the unnamed source of being.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A fixed or enduring designation, contrasted with a temporary or inadequate name.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Points to a name that claims permanence, unlike ordinary labels.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative indicating lack or absence of something.
Sentence Translations (English): Without guilt.
No one knows it.
There is nothing it does not contain.
There is no help for it.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The state of not having a name or, more broadly, of being undifferentiated and unformed.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it denotes a prior, undetermined state, not merely simple negation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The cosmic totality of heaven and earth, often used to mean the universe or the created world.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A cosmological pair, not simply the sky and the ground.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A grammatical particle linking two nouns or a noun phrase to indicate possession, attribution, or relation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Functions grammatically rather than lexically.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese
contextual_sense.Translation (English): of; particle marking possession or relation

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The starting point or first stage of something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The first emergence or source-stage, not merely the start of an action.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks existence or possession.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Used existentially as the counterpart to 無 in this passage.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): All created things; everything in the world.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A cosmological collective term for all beings and phenomena.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): That which gives rise to or generates something; the source from which it comes forth.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means origin or generative source, not a biological mother specifically.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a conclusion or result drawn from what precedes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks logical inference in literary prose.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Continuously or habitually, without interruption.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Indicates enduring regularity, not mere frequency.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Wishing, craving, or seeking after something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Usually means active wanting, often with a moral or spiritual implication.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces purpose or means.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Links an intended action to its aim.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese
contextual_sense.Translation (English): so as to; in order to

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To look at or examine attentively.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often implies reflective observation rather than casual looking.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Third-person possessive or attributive pronoun modifying a noun.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks possession or reference without specifying gender or number.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The elusive, finely hidden character of reality that can only be apprehended through non-desiring observation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Not mere cleverness; it points to the hidden depth of the Dao.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A boundary or frontier line separating regions.
Sentence Translations (English): Guard the border.
Beyond the frontier there is much wind.
It reaches the boundary.
He crosses the frontier and enters.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The outer edge, boundary line, or reach of something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here the sense is of visible limits or outlines, in contrast with 妙.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A demonstrative referring to something near at hand or just mentioned.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Points to the immediately discussed pair.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A numeral-like word meaning two together or both sides of a pair.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emphasizes a pair taken together.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A nominalizing particle or pronoun-like suffix referring to a preceding phrase.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Turns a phrase into a substantive reference.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Identical or sharing the same nature or source.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Highlights sameness beneath difference.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To go out from a source or originate.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often means origin or emergence, not simple physical exit alone.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A coordinating conjunction linking clauses or contrasting them.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Connects with either sequence or contrast, depending on context.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Not the same; distinct in kind, name, or appearance.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks distinction rather than opposition in a strong sense.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To refer to something by a certain name or description.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Used for naming or designation, not mere saying.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Deeply hidden, obscure, and unfathomable in nature.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests depth and hiddenness rather than simple darkness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates repetition or additional degree.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it intensifies the preceding term.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A collective quantifier meaning numerous or the whole group.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emphasizes multiplicity or the mass of things.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An entrance or opening providing access.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Metaphorically the entrance or key point to understanding.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The whole world or realm of human society under the sky.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A political-cosmological totality, not merely 'the world' in a modern sense.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Every member of a set; without exception.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Universal quantification.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To know, perceive, or recognize something as true or real.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Cognitive awareness or recognition.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having attractive or pleasing appearance or quality.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is aesthetic value understood as judged beauty.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To carry out an action or engage in conduct.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): General verbal sense of doing or acting.
Sentence Translations (English): A person should have something to do.
A gentleman does not act recklessly.
Act only in doing good.
What he does is very easy.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To serve as or to turn into something in predicative or resultative use.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this formula it links a thing with the predicate that follows.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a resulting conclusion, often with a slight demonstrative force.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks the consequence just stated, sometimes with a pointed 'this is why' feel.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To dislike strongly or hold in aversion.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A verbal sense distinct from the adjective 'bad'.
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone hates it.
A gentleman does not hate people.
He dislikes the name of it.
What all together hate.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally or qualitatively bad, opposed to good.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage, the opposite of 美 as a value judgment.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks completion or an immediate resulting state.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it closes the judgment with a sense of finality.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally good, proper, or beneficial.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it is a value term, parallel to 美.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative prefix or particle attached to an adjective or verb to mark its opposite.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Standard negation before adjectives and verbs.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Reciprocal marker showing that two sides act upon one another.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Indicates reciprocal relation between paired terms.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To produce, generate, or bring about something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Covers mutual generation or becoming, not biological birth alone.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A pair of opposites used to describe relative degree of difficulty.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A paired contrast, not a single fixed compound.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To bring something to completion or make it come about.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means reciprocal completion or support.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A pair of opposites referring to length in contrast.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A relative comparison, not an abstract compound.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To set things against each other for comparison.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Implies weighing or comparing two things side by side.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A pair of opposites referring to vertical or rank-based position.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A relational contrast of position or status.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To incline, lean, or cause to slant in relation to something else.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it suggests mutual leaning or mutual dependence.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Audible tones, from musical notes to general sounds.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Pairs musical tones with ordinary sound as a sonic category.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To match, blend, or be in harmony with something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is reciprocal accord among sounds or things.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The temporal or spatial relation of being earlier and later, front and back.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A paired relational contrast, often order or sequence.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To come after or accompany by following behind.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Implies being in sequence or accompanying movement.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a conclusion or resulting action.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A set inferential phrase, not a simple demonstrative.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person of profound wisdom and exemplary moral authority, especially in political or philosophical discourse.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The ideal ruler-sage implied by Daoist political thought.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi / Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To occupy oneself with or handle a matter in a certain way.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means to handle or undertake the matter of non-action.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese
contextual_sense.Translation (English): manage; dwell in; conduct oneself in

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An action, business, or undertaking.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A concrete matter or undertaking, not an abstract event only.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move on foot or proceed.
Sentence Translations (English): He walks along the road.
He goes slowly onward.
He walks as far as the gate.
If one does not go, one stops.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To perform or put into effect a teaching, policy, or conduct.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means acting in accordance with a teaching, not merely walking.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text
